title: Claude Code’s auto mode will be on by default, Anthropic confirms
excerpt: The idea is to speed up your coding even more.
content_html:
Anthropic's AI programming tool just made a somewhat big change.

In a blog post, Anthropic announced that "auto mode" will, going forward, be turned on by default in Claude Code for anyone with a Pro, Max, or Team account. The change takes effect on Aug. 14, though you might get a prompt asking if you want to turn on auto mode depending on what settings you've chosen for yourself.

Mashable Light Speed

This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.

For the uninitiated (read: me), auto mode in Claude Code stops asking for human prompts at each step of the development process, instead giving the AI agent permission to proceed on its own unless the action it's taking would be destructive or impossible to reverse. That sounds like it'd be difficult to trust as a programmer, but Anthropic claims that in testing, auto mode caught 89 percent of harmful actions, while real humans only caught 13.6 percent.

You May Also Like

And now, that will be the out-of-the-box experience for Claude Code users. As always, though, you can still turn it off.

content_html_zh:
Anthropic的AI编程工具刚刚做了一些大的改变。

Anthropic 在一篇博客文章中宣布，今后，任何拥有 Pro、Max 或 Team 帐户的人都将在 Claude Code 中默认打开“自动模式”。 此更改将于 8 月 14 日生效，不过您可能会收到提示，询问您是否要打开自动模式，具体取决于您为自己选择的设置。

对于外行（请阅读：我）来说，Claude Code 中的自动模式不再在开发过程的每个步骤中要求人工提示，而是允许人工智能代理自行继续，除非它所采取的操作具有破坏性或无法逆转。 作为一名程序员，这听起来似乎很难让人相信，但 Anthropic 声称，在测试中，自动模式捕获了 89% 的有害行为，而真正的人类只能捕获 13.6%。
